question_text: A GenAI microservice must run in containers with NO server or cluster management, scaling to zero between sporadic requests, while still allowing a custom container image. Which compute option best matches these requirements?

options.text: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate — serverless containers with no cluster/EC2 management
Amazon EKS on self-managed EC2 nodes
A single large EC2 instance running Docker manually

explanation: ECS on Fargate runs containers serverlessly — no EC2/cluster to manage, pay per running task, supports custom images — ideal for sporadic microservices. EKS on self-managed nodes adds Kubernetes and node management overhead; a manual EC2+Docker box requires you to manage the host and scaling; AWS Batch targets batch/HPC job queues, not always-available microservices.
source_topic: ECS on Fargate for serverless GenAI containers

question_text: A pipeline must run thousands of independent, long-running document-processing jobs that each call an FM, with automatic queueing and provisioning of compute as jobs complete. Which AWS service is purpose-built to orchestrate this batch workload?

options.text: AWS Batch — managed batch job queueing and compute provisioning

explanation: AWS Batch manages job queues and dynamically provisions/scales compute (EC2 or Fargate) to run large numbers of independent batch jobs — a natural fit for bulk FM-processing pipelines. App Runner is for always-on web apps/APIs; API Gateway fronts request/response APIs; Cognito handles user authentication.
source_topic: AWS Batch for large-scale GenAI batch jobs

topic: App Runner for GenAI web apps
question_text: A team wants to deploy a containerised GenAI web API directly from a source image with automatic load balancing, TLS, and scaling — without configuring ECS clusters, load balancers, or Kubernetes. Which service offers this simplest fully-managed container web deployment?
explanation: AWS App Runner deploys a container or source repo as a scalable web service with built-in load balancing, TLS, and autoscaling and the least operational setup. EKS requires Kubernetes management; AWS Batch is for batch jobs, not web serving; EC2 Auto Scaling groups require you to manage instances and load balancers yourself.
source_topic: AWS App Runner for managed container web apps

question_text: During traffic spikes, an FM-processing service is overwhelmed and drops requests. The team wants to buffer incoming work so workers can process it at a sustainable rate without losing requests. Which service provides this durable buffering/decoupling?

options.text: Amazon SQS — a durable queue that buffers requests for asynchronous worker processing

explanation: Amazon SQS durably buffers requests so downstream FM workers consume them at a controlled rate, absorbing spikes and preventing loss — the classic decoupling pattern (often with a dead-letter queue for failures). Route 53 is DNS, CloudFront is a CDN, and KMS is key management — none provide request buffering.
source_topic: Amazon SQS buffering for FM inference spikes

question_text: When an asynchronous FM document-processing job finishes, the system must notify multiple independent subscribers (an email alert, a Lambda post-processor, and an SQS queue) at once. Which service implements this pub/sub fan-out?

options.text: Amazon SNS — publish once, fan out to multiple subscribers (email, Lambda, SQS)

explanation: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub service: a single published message fans out to many subscribers such as email, Lambda functions, and SQS queues — ideal for broadcasting job-completion events. Aurora is a database, Secrets Manager stores secrets, and OpenSearch is a search/analytics engine — none provide pub/sub fan-out.
source_topic: Amazon SNS fan-out for job completion events
